---
title: Build a Marfa plugin
description: Install a Marfa plugin from its source folder, with a type, guidance, a setting and a connector written with the kit, and see the connector recorded.
job: A builder installs a Marfa plugin from its source folder.
kind: tutorial
---

- **You'll build** Concerts, a Marfa plugin whose connector reads a JSON list of tickets. This is a plugin an owner installs, from the [plugins repository](https://github.com/withmarfa/plugins), not the [Marfa plugin for agents](/connect-your-agent).
- **You need** Node.js 22.12 or later, pnpm, and a checkout of that repository on `main`, with the kit built (`pnpm install && pnpm exec tsc -b kit` from the checkout). Put the `concerts` folder next to it, so the kit is at `../plugins/kit`. You also need the `marfa` CLI signed in to your instance, as the [Quickstart](/quickstart) leaves you.
- **You'll have** the plugin installed, its type and guidance stored, and its connector recorded with no host. A host will mint the key and start the connector. This tutorial stops before that, because Marfa doesn't publish a host yet.

<Steps paged>
<Step>

### Write the plugin folder

The folder you install holds `plugin.json`, the type, and the type's guidance. The connector program stays beside that folder.

```json title="plugin/plugin.json"
{
  "name": "concerts",
  "title": "Concerts",
  "description": "Concert tickets from a JSON list.",
  "mark": "lucide:ticket",
  "maker": "North Line",
  "marfa": "0.0.101",
  "connector": {
    "source": "concerts",
    "source_name": "Concerts",
    "source_mark": "lucide:ticket",
    "kinds": [
      { "name": "ticket", "type": "concerts.ticket", "direction": "in" }
    ],
    "settings": [
      {
        "name": "concert_list",
        "label": "Ticket list address",
        "kind": "text",
        "required": true
      }
    ],
    "runs": { "on": "host" }
  }
}
```

`concerts` is the plugin's name and the source the tickets are written under. `concert_list` is the address of the JSON list. The [plugin format](/reference/plugin-format#connector) is the rest of the file.

```json title="plugin/types/concerts.ticket.json"
{
  "id": "concerts.ticket",
  "label": "Concert ticket",
  "description": "A ticket from a concert list, with the concert's own id and title.",
  "fields": {
    "concert_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "required": true,
      "description": "The concert's id on the list."
    },
    "title": {
      "type": "string",
      "required": true,
      "description": "The concert's name."
    }
  },
  "display_hints": { "title_field": "title" }
}
```

The file beside it is the guidance a person reads with the type:

```md title="plugin/types/concerts.ticket.md"
**Use for:** a ticket on a concert list the connector reads, one item for each concert.

**Not for:** work you track yourself, which is a `common.ticket` kind, or an event you keep yourself, which is a `core.event`.

**Body:** `title` is the concert's name. `concert_id` is the id the list gives that concert, and the connector finds the item by it.
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Write the connector

The program uses the [connector kit](/reference/connector-kit). `run` fetches the list and hands each ticket to `upsert`. Pass `connector` itself to `main`, not `connector()`, so each run is built from the settings Marfa holds.

```json title="package.json"
{
  "name": "concerts",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "dependencies": {
    "@withmarfa/connector": "file:../plugins/kit"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "typescript": "5.9.3"
  }
}
```

```json title="tsconfig.json"
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "es2022",
    "module": "nodenext",
    "moduleResolution": "nodenext",
    "strict": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "resolveJsonModule": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true
  },
  "include": ["src"]
}
```

```ts title="src/definition.ts"
import { defineConnector, type TypeDefinition } from "@withmarfa/connector";
import ticket from "../plugin/types/concerts.ticket.json" with { type: "json" };

const type = ticket as TypeDefinition;
export function connector() {
  return defineConnector({
    name: "concerts",
    title: "Concerts",
    mark: "lucide:ticket",
    maker: "North Line",
    description: "Concert tickets from a JSON list.",
    source: "concerts",
    sourceName: "Concerts",
    sourceMark: "lucide:ticket",
    types: [{ name: "ticket", direction: "in", type, fields: ["concert_id", "title"] }],
    settings: [{ name: "concert_list", label: "Ticket list address", kind: "text", required: true }],
    async run({ env, signal, upsert }) {
      const rows = (await fetch(env.concert_list, { signal }).then((r) => r.json())) as { id: string; title: string }[];
      await upsert(type.id, rows.map((row) => ({
        source_id: row.id,
        properties: { concert_id: row.id, title: row.title },
      })));
    },
  });
}
```

```ts title="src/main.ts"
import { main } from "@withmarfa/connector";
import { connector } from "./definition.js";

await main(connector);
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Typecheck it

From the `concerts` folder, install the kit and typecheck the program. `tsc` prints nothing when the connector matches the kit.

<Terminal>

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm exec tsc --noEmit
```

```text
+ @withmarfa/connector file:../plugins/kit
+ typescript 5.9.3
```

</Terminal>

</Step>
<Step>

### Check the plugin folder

Check judges the folder the way an install would, and talks to no server:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa plugins check plugin
```

```text
types/concerts.ticket.json: ok
the plugin passes
```

</Terminal>

</Step>
<Step>

### Install it

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa plugins install plugin
```

```text
built plugin at 0.0.0, SHA-256 d1e07e22cc3c591e61b418f1bf4ad2a671c768f926f1520c096019c90e82df77
installed concerts 0.0.0 with 1 type; its connector runs on no host yet: marfa plugins assign concerts --host `host`
```

</Terminal>

The type is installed with its guidance. The last words of that line name a host. Marfa doesn't publish one yet, so the connector stays recorded with no host.

</Step>
<Step>

### See the connector recorded

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa plugins get concerts
```

```text
connector.source                concerts
connector.source_name           Concerts
connector.kinds[0].name         ticket
connector.kinds[0].type         concerts.ticket
connector.kinds[0].direction    in
connector.settings[0].name      concert_list
connector.runs.on               host
connector_host                  -
```

</Terminal>

The answer has more fields than this. `connector_host` is empty. The install recorded the connector. It did not register a running process: that happens when a host starts the kit with a key the host minted.

</Step>
<Step>

### Leave the run to a host

A host mints a key for this connector and starts the process with `MARFA_API_URL`, that key, and telemetry settings. The kit reads `concert_list` from Marfa at the start of the run. [Make a connector follow changes](/build/connector-follow-changes) stores the address. The [connector kit](/reference/connector-kit) is what the process checks the key against, and [Write a connector without the kit](/build/connector-without-the-kit) is the same run on the API.

The [kit's README](https://github.com/withmarfa/plugins/blob/main/kit/README.md) is the reference for the rest of the kit: archiving what the vendor dropped, connections, state, carrying changes back with `onChange`, and webhooks.

  <Card title="Connector kit" href="/reference/connector-kit">The key, the settings and the exit codes.</Card>
</Cards>

</Step>
</Steps>
